This is a bounded fix. The goal is to ensure a collision never leaves a half-renamed directory; existing constraints are synchronous Node built-ins, one directory, and script-friendly output.

One behavior needs deciding: when any target name already exists, should the command:

1. Abort before renaming anything and report every collision — recommended for predictable, repeatable runs.
2. Skip colliding files and rename the rest.
3. Automatically choose alternative target names.

Which behavior do you want?

Design: add a preflight validation step before `applyRenames` performs any filesystem changes. It will collect all target conflicts—including duplicate targets within the plan—and ignore exact no-op entries where source and target are identical. If conflicts exist, it will throw one aggregate error listing every conflicting target; nothing will be renamed.

The CLI will catch this expected error, print each collision to stderr, and exit nonzero. Successful rename mappings remain on stdout. Tests will use temporary directories to verify multiple collisions are all reported, no files change after rejection, and collision-free/no-op plans still work.

Does this design look right?

Implemented the collision-safe renamer.

- Preflights the entire rename plan before changing files.
- Reports every collision and exits nonzero.
- Detects case-insensitive clashes.
- Detects duplicate targets within a plan.
- Treats exact source/target matches as no-ops, making repeated runs safe.
- Added coverage for all new behavior.
